newsitem.title: UK: Reed plays down impact of U.S. court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Reed plays down impact of U.S. court ruling.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publisher Reed Elsevier on Thursday played down the significance of a recent U.S. court decision relating to legal publisher West Publishing, saying the ruling would have only a "minimal impact" on Reed's Lexis-Nexis unit.

Reports of the ruling, along with a downgrade on Reed shares by a major brokerage, sent Reed Elsevier shares sharply lower in early trading on Thursday. By 1446 the stock was down 21p at 604-1/2 in heavy trade of 9.2 million shares.

In a statement, Reed said: "The decision of the New York Federal Court finding the West Publishing company ceases to enjoy protection in the text of federal court decisions, while clearly rebuffing West's long asserted right to protection, will have minimal impact on Reed Elsevier and its electronic publishing unit, Lexis-Nexis, even if the decision is upheld on appeal."
"The value that large legal publishers like Lexis-Nexis offer the legal community extends far beyone the text of legal decisions," the company said.

"The breadth and depth of the legal information offerings, the editorial enhancements and the search and navigation systems...are the foundation of Lexis-Nexis, which is unaffected by the recent West decision."

Under the ruling, only West's notes and other added material retail are allowed copyright protection, meaning that rival publishers can copy decisions in West law books into their computers and then issue them in book or electronic form.

A report in the New York Times said the ruling was expected to drive down the price of legal research in the United States. West was acquired last year by publishing group Thomson Corporation for $1.4 billion.
The paper said Thomson was planning to appeal against the ruling.
Separately, analysts at Merrill Lynch downgraded their rating on the Reed to "accumulate" from "buy" following a briefing with executives from the company, dealers said.

There was market talk that at least one other major brokerage had lowered its earnings expectations for the media and publishing group, though market sources declined to confirm that the move was related to the U.S. ruling.
